input: words contains ASCII lowercase strings and chars is an ASCII lowercase string. Empty strings/list are accepted. Sum T of all word lengths is a safe integer. Each word receives its own fresh supply of chars. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. Python integer inputs are plain int, excluding bool.
return: Sum of lengths of words that can be formed without using any character more times than it occurs in chars. Duplicate word occurrences contribute independently.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; only private working state is used. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: All histogram counts fit string lengths and accumulated result is at most T. Supply is not consumed between different words. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(len(chars)+T+26*W+1) time and O(26) auxiliary space for W words, with a constant number of26-entry histograms, including transient overlap while replacing a prior histogram. Per-word histogram allocation and Python all-generator/JS loop work are counted. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
